summary: CCC-era summit lookout on Baboquivari Peak (Pima County, AZ), abandoned and gone; steel, concrete and wood remnants remain on the summit; permit-based access.

facts.status_note: Only a few steel supports, concrete foundations and wooden piles remain on the summit, per a climbing guide
facts.agency: Civilian Conservation Corps, Indian Division (built); summit on Papago Indian Reservation land

access.note: Summit is on Papago Indian Reservation land; a climbing page says a permit can be downloaded; the standard route is technical and has seen several accidents

visit.trail_note: Old wooden ladders have rotted and are not safe to rely on; the standard summit route is a technical climb

events.note: Telephone booth on the summit, reported in a September 1938 newspaper item
Visitor found the ranger cabin on the summit tumble-down (May 1947 account)
Article dated October 25, 1974 says the fire lookout was judged not needed after a few years and the ladder system was abandoned

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1947 account describes a ranger cabin on the summit; the climbing guide says the CCC erected a fire lookout tower there. The story reports both descriptions.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 222.5 is not supported by any source read; the 1947 account gives the peak as 7,730 feet, so the brief value looks like a different measure and was dropped from facts. Brief kind 'ground' conflicts with sources that describe a summit lookout tower or ranger cabin; left for the editor. The build year is only given as the 1930s, so no dated build event is recorded. The CCC campground cabin is a different structure and is not used for the lookout. No Forest Service, tribal or CCC camp record was reached.
